A hands-on class on doing data science in R: eight **data-wrangling** parts
(Introduction → Manipulate Data Types) and an **exploratory data analysis**
extension covering hypothesis testing, linear modeling and principal component
analysis. The data-wrangling slides are Keynote decks exported to PDF; the EDA
slides are interactive Quarto *revealjs* decks. Every part pairs its slides
with a Quarto exercise file you can open and work through.

This material builds on the work of [Garrett
Grolemund](https://www.linkedin.com/in/garrett-grolemund-49328411/) from
[posit](https://posit.co), reusing part of his
[tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org)-related workshop material from
<https://github.com/rstudio-education/remaster-the-tidyverse> under the
[Creative Commons BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)
license.

## Prerequisites

- R: <https://www.r-project.org>
- RStudio or Positron: <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/> / <https://positron.posit.co/download.html>
- Quarto: <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>
- Tidyverse: <https://www.tidyverse.org>

## R packages

- Data sets: `{babynames}` (baby-name frequency, US 1880–2017), `{nycflights13}` (2013 NYC flight records).
- Data wrangling: `{janitor}`, `{skimr}`.
- Extra visualization: `{ggcorrplot}`, `{ggfortify}`, `{plotly}`.
- Reporting: `{DT}` (DataTables), `{gt}`, `{kableExtra}`.
- Model summaries: `{broom}`.
- PCA: `{FactoMineR}`, `{factoextra}`, `{corrplot}`, `{viridis}`, `{huxtable}`, `{umap}`.
